_about: What each page of the Brain Viewer is for, in plain words. One entry per route in serve.py's PAGES. The question mark button on every page shows its own entry; the home page shows this one plus a line per widget it is carrying. Written for a person who has just opened the app, so no ids, no codes, no jargon. Since 2026-10-16 the file also carries the glossary (the `glossary` key): every word the app uses, grouped, with the ledger's kinds and tags among them. Since 2026-10-26 each page's entry carries `workflow`, a typical workflow in three steps, and the `widgets` key carries one card per instrument of the board, by the widget's file name; the Manual page (/manual) draws both, with the folder and skill readmes, as the manual of the brain and the viewer.

/.what: The page the viewer opens on, and the one place an item is answered, closed or put off. It runs in the order of the day. Up first: one to three items the session picked for you to answer now, each with a line on why it is up here. Under it, when the viewer has changed or a run has written a note since your last visit, what changed and the notes, each one press away. Then the calls: the one now or next with its prep, and the one just held with a press to what came out of it. Then the work in progress as one strip of instruments, one per project, each with your next move on it as its one press. Then what is due today beside what is new since you last looked. Then the folds: the backlog with its count, what you put on hold, what others owe today, what waits on another person, the transcripts that landed today, what closed, and what was built. Every press is saved at once and waits for the Send press at the bottom right, for you leaving the viewer, or for a few quiet minutes, then goes to the session; the Settings page changes that.

parts.name: Up first
parts.line: The first band: one to three of your items the session picked, drawn as full cards with their presses and one small line each saying why it is up here, so that what most needs an answer is the first thing on the page. The session writes the pick at its start and after every batch of your answers; when it has not written one today, the page picks for itself: a question with named choices that is new since you last looked, then anything due today, then an item blocking another. An item drawn here is not drawn again below.

parts.name: Changed since you last looked
parts.line: Under Up first, drawn only when there is something in it. While the viewer runs a version you have not marked seen: the version it is now and the title of what changed, one line for each change, where to see it, and two presses. Read what's new opens the viewer's what's-new page in the Reader, newest day first. Seen marks this version seen: the band folds to one line, Viewer and its version, seen, for the rest of the day, and the dot on more in the header goes. Under it, Overnight: the notes the development run, the night agent and the brain engineer wrote since your last visit, each one press to the Reader by its title, the development run's delivery note first. In a team copy the band shows the viewer's change only.

parts.name: Calls
parts.line: The call now or next as the lead card with its prep, and a call just held with a press to what came out of it (its transcript or report once it is in the brain), or add the transcript while nothing is. A block on the calendar, such as therapy or an all-day marker, is not a call and is not drawn here. The header counts today's calls and names the next one.

parts.name: In progress
parts.line: One strip of instruments, one per project the sessions register as being worked on, newest first: the project's name, a dot and when it was last touched, one line of state, how many of your items are open on it, and your next move on it as the one press: of your items registered on it and those that link its thread, the one its thread draws first. Pressing an instrument, or its next move's words, opens that item on its thread, where the page scrolls to it and it flashes, then stays outlined; an item on no thread opens on its own. One with nothing of yours on it opens the project's page. Nothing else of the project is drawn here; its notes, files and other items live on its own page.

parts.name: Due today and New since you last looked
parts.line: Two columns, one at phone width: what is due today, and what is new since your last visit, each row marked with what changed and when, each with its presses and an undo. A pick, a choice between pages to look at, carries Compare, which opens the options side by side. An item already drawn up first or as a project's next move is not drawn again. Under them the backlog, everything older or dated later, folded under one line with its count.

parts.name: Built, to look at
parts.line: The three newest things built in the brain, a site or a page, each by its name. Press one and the page itself opens in a new tab, full window. All goes to the Artifacts page with every one of them. With nothing built, the band is not drawn.

parts.name: On hold
parts.line: Your tasks put down for later, folded at the end of the list with their count, each with the day it comes back on its own; bring back returns one now. A task held because it waits on a person it names is under Waiting on others instead.

parts.name: Might annoy you
parts.line: Up to three cards, each something in the brain's own output that resembles one you have reacted to before: the moment quoted, then the pattern it resembles with its rule. Press Annoying or Not annoying, or write a comment; the answer goes into the record of how you work and reaches the session like any other press. With no card open, the band is not drawn.

parts.name: Clear what's settled
parts.line: Reads each open question and task of yours against the brain since it was written, and closes or rewrites what has moved. Items from calls older than two weeks wait for this pass before the list shows them again.

parts.name: To approve in the app
parts.line: One row per call whose action items wait for approval in the app, at the end of the backlog, or with what is new when the call came after your last visit: approve all, skip until tomorrow, or open the items one by one.

parts.name: Others owe today
parts.line: What is due today or earlier on someone else, oldest first; Claude's own are one line with their count. Nothing of yours is here: what you put on hold is under On hold.

parts.name: Calls and transcripts
parts.line: Today's calls, each row one press to its call page (the prep as boxes to tick, and the notes box); join is its own press, the prep's state is the word at the right (a skeleton says so), and its purpose shows in full. Then what landed in the transcript folders, each by its title.

parts.name: A picture in a note
parts.line: A note can carry a picture. Paste one into an item's note box: it is kept in the brain and the box shows where, and once the note is written the picture is drawn under the note's words. Writing a picture's place in the brain, or a link to it, in a note does the same. A press on the picture opens it in the image viewer. A web address stays a link. In a team copy a pasted picture is not kept (a copy adds no files); a picture already in the copy can be linked.

parts.name: What's new
parts.line: The first entry under more in the list of pages, on every page: the viewer's what's-new page, what changed day by day in plain words, opened in the Reader. While the viewer runs a version you have not marked seen, a dot sits on more and beside the link; Seen on Today's Changed since you last looked band takes it away. On a phone more is under menu, and the menu press carries the dot.

parts.name: On a phone
parts.line: Below 600 pixels wide the header is one line: back, the page's name and menu. Menu unfolds the rest under that line (the day, the search, this page's own controls, the list of pages, with what's new first under more, and the question mark); a press anywhere else, or Escape, folds it again. While the viewer has changed and you have not pressed Seen, the menu press carries a dot.

workflow: Answer what is under Up first: each card carries its presses and a line saying why it is up there.
When a call's hour comes, open it from the calls band and read Decide before first.
Press Send at the bottom right when you are done, or just leave the viewer: what you pressed reaches the session.

/home.what: The board: instruments only. The date across the top with the day's line under it; beside it the slot you choose an instrument for (the day as a band with today's calls on it, one project as the track of its stages, or the week as seven columns). On the right the sun carries the sessions running right now and the moon says whether the night agent ran. Under that: one line for the call in front of you, which opens Today, the chat, the people your week is made of, the countdowns, what moved in the brain, the brain wired to everything it exchanges anything with, and a lamp for every part that runs on its own. Nothing is answered or closed here: that is Today, the page the viewer opens on. The edit button in the top right rearranges all of it: drag an instrument, make it a third, a half, two thirds or the full width, let it stand two rows tall, switch one off, or add one that is off. What you set is saved for you and comes back on any browser. Along the foot of the board, one lamp per status file: lit when it was written in the last three days, dim when older, red when it cannot be read or a check in it failed. Press one to read it.

parts.name: The header
parts.line: The date, a clock, the sessions running right now as dots going round the sun, and the moon beside it: lit when the night agent ran last night, and as full as the number of the last seven nights it ran. The middle of the header is yours to choose: press day, project or week in its corner. Day is a band from seven in the morning to seven at night with each call a block on it and a gold line where the hour is. Project draws one project as a track of its stages, the done ones filled and the one you are on lit, with a chooser for which project. Week is seven narrow columns with the calls on them and today marked.

parts.name: Mantra
parts.line: One line a day under the date, picked from the date itself so it is the same all day and changes at midnight. Hover it for next, which shows another of today's lines, and add, which puts a line of your own into the pool everyone on the team draws from.

parts.name: Next
parts.line: One line: when the next call is, what it is and who is on it, and a link to Today's calls, where the join press and the prep are.

parts.name: Chat
parts.line: The conversation, under Next. The last thing you asked and the answer it gave, the box to send the next message with Enter, a new one on a press, a chooser in its corner for which conversation you are in, and a lit dot for each one with a turn running when more than one is. The whole thread, with its tool calls, is one link away.

parts.name: People
parts.line: Everyone on your calendar between today and seven days out together with everyone the open items still name, in one of two forms you press for in its corner. In graph they are bubbles around the mark of the brain, moving under the same physics as the bubbles on the map: the line to the middle is heavier the more calls and open items tie a person there, two people sitting on the same call are threaded to each other, and anyone you speak to inside two days is in the burgundy. Drag a bubble and the rest answer, drag the ground to move the view, wheel to zoom, hover for when you next speak and how much is open, press to open the prep for that call or their card. The three words beside the forms choose what stands in the middle: the sun, Saturn or Venus. In list they are a roll of names that drifts upward on its own, with the next call beside each one, and it stops the moment you put the pointer on it.

parts.name: Moved
parts.line: What changed in the brain, newest first, grouped by the hour, in the words of whoever changed it.

parts.name: Horizon
parts.line: Days left to each milestone this brain sets in its horizon file, in one of two forms you press for in its corner: numerals, one count per milestone with a bar for how far through the run today is, or road, the whole run drawn as one track from its start day to the last milestone with each milestone marked on it, every step the ledgers give a day set where its day falls, and a marker at today with the count to the next milestone above it. With no horizon file it says so in one line.

parts.name: Flow
parts.line: The brain in the middle and the eight things it exchanges anything with around it: the ProspectForge app, the onboarding API, the calendar, GitHub, Obsidian Sync, the team copy, the scheduled agents and your Claude Code sessions. A wire is bright when it carried something in the last day, and a gold dot runs along it the moment something crosses, because it is watching the brain's log as it is written. Hover a node for the last thing that moved there, press one to open its page, or expand it to the full width.

parts.name: System
parts.line: A lamp for every part of this brain that runs on its own, with the last time each one ran under it: the calendar read, the week file, the sync with the ProspectForge app, the night agent, the weekly librarian, git, and this app. Green is inside its rhythm, gold has missed a turn, red is overdue or has never run.

parts.name: Space, the command line, the sundial, the constellation and the rest
parts.line: Off the board and waiting in the add strip when you press edit, which becomes a small window of its own once you scroll past it: carry it anywhere by the bar across its top, pull the bottom right corner to make it bigger, and it opens where you left it next time. Space is a blank one: it draws nothing and holds a gap open wherever you put it. The command line is one message to the main agent with no conversation around it. Tally is the three counts of the day in a form you choose. The sundial is the older drawing of the day as an arc, and the constellation is the brain drawn as projects, threads and people around the sun.

parts.name: The status lamps
parts.line: One lamp per part of the brain that writes a file about its own state. Press one to read the file.

workflow: Look at the board for the shape of the day: the call in front of you, the people of your week, what moved.
Press edit to turn an instrument on or off, drag it to a new place, or make it wider.
Press done: the board is saved as yours, and an update never moves it.

/index.html.what: The same page as the one the viewer opens on, Today, reached by its other address.

parts.name: Built, to look at
parts.line: The three newest things built in the brain, a site or a page, each by its name. Press one and the page itself opens in a new tab, full window. All goes to the Artifacts page with every one of them. With nothing built, the band is not drawn.

parts.name: Today
parts.line: Everything yours to do, what is new since you last looked first, today's calls and what landed. The board of instruments is at /home.

/today.what: The page the viewer opens on, and the one place an item is answered, closed or put off. It runs from the top: Up first, the one to three items picked for you to answer now, each with why it is up there; under it, Changed since you last looked, when the viewer has changed or a run has written a note since your last visit; then the calls as the day has them; then In progress, one instrument for each piece of work being made; then Due today beside New since you last looked; then the backlog, what is on hold and the rest of the day, each folded under one line with its count. An item is drawn once on the page, in the first place it belongs. Every press is saved at once, goes to the session when you send it, leave the viewer or stop pressing for a few minutes, and can be taken back for the rest of the day. A task that carries steps draws them under its words as a numbered list with a tick box each, before the chips and the note; a tick is a press like any other, and once every step is ticked, done is the card's lead press. A long note sits under the steps folded to its first line, with a more press that opens it. Your replies and what Claude wrote back are a list under the item's note, you then Claude, the latest open and the earlier ones folded; the reply press leaves the item as it is. On a step, the box is the only tick; a step that names a place links it in its words and carries an open press at its right. In a team copy it opens on the From band: what the brain's owner sent you (the questions put to you with their presses, the files new since you last looked, the notes written for you) and one press that sends your answers.

parts.name: Up first
parts.line: The first band: one to three of your items as full cards with their presses, each with one line saying why it is up here, so what needs answering is the first thing on the page. A session picks them, and the evening run picks them for the next morning; the header says who picked them and when. On a day nothing has been picked, or once what was picked is done, the viewer ranks its own: a question with named choices that is new since you last looked, then what is due today, then what other work waits on. An item opened from another page sits here first. Clear what's settled is in this band's header.

parts.name: Changed since you last looked
parts.line: Under Up first, drawn only when there is something in it. While the viewer runs a version you have not marked seen: the version it is now and the title of what changed, one line for each change, where to see it, and two presses. Read what's new opens the viewer's what's-new page in the Reader, newest day first. Seen marks this version seen: the band folds to one line, Viewer and its version, seen, for the rest of the day, and the dot on more in the header goes. Under it, Overnight: the notes the development run, the night agent and the brain engineer wrote since your last visit, each one press to the Reader by its title, the development run's delivery note first. In a team copy the band shows the viewer's change only.

parts.name: Calls
parts.line: The calls as on the day. The call just held and the call now or next are the lead cards: the one held carries a press to what came out of it, the report or the transcript once its recording is in the brain, and add the transcript while nothing is in the brain yet (the file picker, then its call page); the one now or next carries its prep and its join press. With no call left today, the next one on the calendar is the next card, with its day. The day's other calls are rows under them, each one press to its call page. A block, such as therapy, an all-day marker or an event with nobody else on it, is never a call and is not drawn here.

parts.name: In progress
parts.line: One strip of instruments, one for each piece of work being made, the newest first: its name, how fresh it is (a dot and when it was last touched), one line on where it stands, the count of your open items on it, and your next move on it as the one press that item carries (an answer, done, Take the survey or Compare). The items counted are yours registered on it and yours that link its thread, and the next move is the one its thread draws first: the thread's own first, then what other work waits on, the soonest due, the newest. Pressing an instrument, or its next move's words, opens that item, question or task, on its thread: the page scrolls to it and it flashes, then stays outlined; an item on no thread opens on its own and flashes there. An instrument with nothing of yours on it opens the project's page, where its notes, its files and its other items are. With nothing registered as in progress, the strip is not drawn.

parts.name: Due today
parts.line: Beside New since you last looked, and above it at phone width: what of yours is due today or back from a hold today and is not drawn higher up, each with its presses; every press has an undo for the rest of the day.

parts.name: New since you last looked
parts.line: What was filed for you, answered, noted, handed to you, come back to you or changed since your previous visit, newest first, each marked new with what changed and when; a reload inside ten minutes is the same visit, so the marks stay. What is drawn in Up first or as an instrument's next move is not drawn again here.

parts.name: Backlog
parts.line: Everything else of yours, folded under one line with its count: past its day, dated later and undated alike, each keeping its date, what holds other work first. One press opens it, and it stays open until you leave the page. Show, Order and Project, inside it, narrow and re-sort it and the On hold fold. A question answers with one of its named presses or in your own words; a task is done, held for three days, or given a note. A survey carries one press, Take the survey; a choice between things to look at leads with Compare, which opens its workspace on them side by side. A survey, a pick and a card from the record of how you work each say in one small line what kind of card they are and what the press does; a test is not listed here (it waits under To try on the from-Claude page) and says what it is only when opened by its own link, which puts it at the top of the page.

parts.name: On hold
parts.line: Your tasks put down for later, folded under the backlog with their count, each with the day it comes back on its own; bring back returns one now. A task held because it waits on a person it names is under Waiting on others instead.

parts.name: Others owe today
parts.line: What is due today or earlier on someone else, oldest first; Claude's own are one line with their count. Nothing of yours is here: what you put on hold is under On hold. Folded, with its count.

parts.name: Waiting on others
parts.line: What another person moves next, each with who and since when, folded with its count: nudge writes on it that you asked, drop closes it with a reason.

parts.name: Transcripts landed today
parts.line: The recordings that landed today, each by its title and whether it has been read in, folded with its count; not drawn on a day nothing landed.

parts.name: Closed today
parts.line: What was done or answered today, folded with its count; each one you pressed carries undo, and an answered question a change of answer.

parts.name: Might annoy you
parts.line: Folded, with its count: up to three cards, each something in the brain's own output that resembles one you have reacted to before: the moment quoted, then the pattern it resembles with its rule. Press Annoying or Not annoying, or write a comment; the answer goes into the record of how you work and reaches the session like any other press. With no card open, the band is not drawn.

parts.name: Built, to look at
parts.line: The newest things built in the brain that are still in play, folded with their count; press one and the page itself opens in a new tab. Everything built goes to the Artifacts page.

parts.name: To approve in the app
parts.line: One row per call whose action items wait for approval in the app, at the end of the backlog, or under New since you last looked when the call came after your last visit: approve all, skip until tomorrow, or open the items one by one.

parts.name: From the brain's owner (in a team copy)
parts.line: Your own questions and tasks with their presses, each with a line on where your last press stands: saved on this computer, waiting, sent, then landed once it is on the item. The send press sends what is saved; it first brings in the newest export from GitHub, and when that clashes with a change committed in this folder it says Not sent and why. Below, each send to your copy since you last looked: what became of your requests, a few sentences on what arrived, the note written for you when there is one, and each file one press to open.

parts.name: Sync with the owner (in a shared copy)
parts.line: In a copy that is the member's own brain (0.96.0), the From band says when the shared files last synced and what moved (sent, came, held back, for the owner to decide), with Sync with <owner> now. A press on a shared task list is saved in place and goes to the owner a moment later on its own; nothing waits for a send. Under each day's section, Your changes says what became of each change she made to a shared file: in the owner's brain, or waiting on his choice because he changed the same lines.

parts.name: Share with <member>
parts.line: In a brain that shares a copy with someone, a task on a list their copy holds carries share with <member> beside done, hold and reply, here, on its thread page and in its workspace. The press puts the task on the From band of their Today, under Shared with you, the next time their copy syncs; the sync starts at once. Once shared, the card says shared with <member>, with stop sharing to take it off. Nothing new goes to them: the task's list already does, and a change to the task reaches them with the list at every sync. A task on a list that stays in your brain, a question, and a task marked private have no press.

parts.name: Messages with <member>
parts.line: In a brain that shares a copy with someone, and in that copy: a fold under Up first holding the messages between the two of you, open when one waits on you. Write in the box at its top. While your viewer runs it checks every ten minutes and when it starts (a message sent while your computer was off is answered when it is back on): the agent on your side answers what the other person asks from the files you share and nothing else, with no tool and no other file, and marks its answer as the agent's; what those files do not answer, or what needs your own decision, it passes to you: the thread waits on you, and in the owner's brain it is also a task on the PF build list, which closes when you reply. A reply to something you asked is an answer, never handed to an agent. The minutes are channel_minutes in your settings (0 turns the checks off).

parts.name: Shared with you (in a shared copy)
parts.line: In the From band, the tasks and threads the owner put in front of you with his share press, newest first, each with the day he shared it. A task is drawn as it stands on your copy of its list, read only: it is his, and he closes it; the line under it says when he has. A thread is one press to its page in your copy. When he stops sharing one, it leaves at the next sync.

parts.name: A picture in a note
parts.line: A note can carry a picture. Paste one into an item's note box: it is kept in the brain and the box shows where, and once the note is written the picture is drawn under the note's words. Writing a picture's place in the brain, or a link to it, in a note does the same. A press on the picture opens it in the image viewer. A web address stays a link. In a team copy a pasted picture is not kept (a copy adds no files); a picture already in the copy can be linked.

parts.name: What's new
parts.line: The first entry under more in the list of pages, on every page: the viewer's what's-new page, what changed day by day in plain words, opened in the Reader. While the viewer runs a version you have not marked seen, a dot sits on more and beside the link; Seen on Today's Changed since you last looked band takes it away. On a phone more is under menu, and the menu press carries the dot.

parts.name: On a phone
parts.line: Below 600 pixels wide the header is one line: back, the page's name and menu. Menu unfolds the rest under that line (the day, the search, this page's own controls, the list of pages, with what's new first under more, and the question mark); a press anywhere else, or Escape, folds it again. While the viewer has changed and you have not pressed Seen, the menu press carries a dot.

workflow: Answer what is under Up first: each card carries its presses and a line saying why it is up there.
When a call's hour comes, open it from the calls band and read Decide before first.
Press Send at the bottom right when you are done, or just leave the viewer: what you pressed reaches the session.

/projects.what: Every project's list of work, read straight off the files that hold it. One project at a time: its milestones, the tasks and questions under each, who owns them, what is blocked and what closed. This is where an item gets sorted into a milestone, answered, ticked off or reopened. At the foot, Every part of the brain lists the registry: each folder and file the brain treats as one unit of work, nested as it nests, with its rules, its runbook and its status file.

parts.name: The project picker
parts.line: One row per project with how much is open on it.

parts.name: Milestones
parts.line: The work grouped the way the project groups it; an Inbox group means not yet sorted.

parts.name: An item
parts.line: Its text, its owner, its date, and the controls to answer, tick, block or hold it.

parts.name: Every part of the brain
parts.line: The registry as a tree, folded. Open a row for what it is, where it lives and the files that govern it.

parts.name: On a phone
parts.line: Below 600 pixels wide the header is one line: back, the page's name and menu. Menu unfolds the rest under that line (the day, the search, this page's own controls, the list of pages, with what's new first under more, and the question mark); a press anywhere else, or Escape, folds it again. While the viewer has changed and you have not pressed Seen, the menu press carries a dot.

workflow: Pick a project at the top.
Read its milestones, and answer a question or tick a task where it stands.
At the foot, open Every part of the brain to see what the project is made of.

/studio.what: The image studio: write a prompt, pick a provider (OpenAI, Gemini, fal.ai, or Flux Krea on this computer's own graphics card through ComfyUI, which costs nothing and needs ComfyUI running) and a model, and the pictures land in a job folder under deliverables/studio (in a team copy, in your own folder, mine/studio) where you mark the ones worth keeping as candidates. Each provider runs on this brain's own key file or its own ComfyUI; one that is off says in plain words what to do to switch it on, and its connections are on the Settings page. The edit button under a picture changes it with the model you picked; the local one redraws the whole picture from your words, keeping its layout.
workflow: Write what you want in the brief, and pick a provider and a model; a provider that is off says how to switch it on.
Make the pictures, and star the ones worth keeping.
Attach the one you want to its task (in a team copy, it stays in your own folder), or change it with the edit press.

/people.what: The people in your world, one card each. What the card says about them, what is open that concerns them, the calls you have had, and the prep for the next one. A prep can be written and edited here. In a team copy it lists the cards the copy holds, read only, with no preps.

parts.name: This week's calls
parts.line: Every call in the calendar this week with someone carded on it: the day and time, each person as a link to their card, and the prep with its state (ready, skeleton, held, no prep yet).

parts.name: Who you talk to weekly
parts.line: The people on a call in two or more of the last four weeks, one line each: a dot per week they spoke, where they stand, the first thing open for you, the next call.

parts.name: Everyone else
parts.line: Folds by relationship (mentees, mentors and their companies, partners, candidates, family, the rest, the standing threads), each with how much is waiting on you.

parts.name: A person
parts.line: Their card read back in the drawer, the items naming them, their transcripts and their preps. Widen at its top opens it to most of the page.

parts.name: Their circle
parts.line: Under a person who holds any reach: the people and companies reachable through them, each with its one line, the opportunities it is attached to with their stage, and where it came up. Open in the drawer, where the edit press changes a line, moves a stage or sets the next move.

parts.name: Opportunities on a card
parts.line: Under the open items in the drawer: each opportunity the person is on, one line with its stage, linking to the opportunities page.

parts.name: The prep editor
parts.line: Write or edit the dated prep for a call, saved where the preps live.

workflow: Look at this week's calls at the top, each with its prep beside it.
Open a person to read their card, what is open about them and the calls you have had.
Write or change the prep for the next call before it starts.

/chat.what: Talk to the brain's agents. The main agent reads the brain and answers, puts a question that outlives the message onto the right project list, and hands project work to sub-agents. A conversation fixed to a project boots from that project's notes and writes only to its list. Each conversation is a real session on this machine, so it can be picked up again later. Above the conversation, one line says how many sessions and sub-agents are running on this machine right now.

parts.name: The rail
parts.line: The main agent, one entry per project, and the conversations you have already had.

parts.name: The thread
parts.line: The answer as it arrives, with the tool calls and sub-agents folded behind one line.

parts.name: The composer
parts.line: Your message, the model to run it on, and what the turn cost.

workflow: Type what you want into the box and press Enter.
Read the answer: anything that outlives the message lands on its project's list.
Pick an earlier conversation on the left to carry it on; the line above the conversation says what is running.

/reader.what: Read one brain document as a page: its headings, its text and its lists in one column, nothing folded. Strike an item, reorder it, edit a section or ask a question about it; every change is written back to the real file. Opens the build document when no file is named.

parts.name: The outline
parts.line: Every heading down the left, indented by level. Press one to go there; the heading you are reading is marked as you scroll. On a phone it sits behind the outline button.

parts.name: Edit and Ask
parts.line: Point at a section and they appear in the margin beside its heading. Edit opens that section's raw text to change it; Ask writes a question about it onto a project list, with a link that opens right back here.

parts.name: The list controls
parts.line: Point at a list item for strike (it stays in the file, struck and dated) and the two arrows (it swaps with its neighbour). Each one rewrites that single line.

parts.name: The agent layer
parts.line: One switch at the top, off to begin with. Off, the parts written for agents are not on the page: the block at the top of the file, the notes in quotes, the status lines, the comments and the dated history sections. On, they sit where they are written, tagged agent. A link that points into one turns it on for that visit.

parts.name: The foot of the outline
parts.line: The open items on the project lists that point at this document, grouped by the heading they name, answerable there; and a search of every brain file, whose hits open here at their line.

parts.name: The Share line
parts.line: Under the document's head, when the brain shares files with someone. In a shared copy: a file from the owner says it is shared and that a save goes to him a moment later; a file you made says Yours: only on this computer, with Share with <owner>, which makes it shared and syncs it. In the owner's brain: a file of a folder he shares says so, with Send to <member> now. A file of a folder that is not shared draws nothing.

workflow: Open a document from any link, or from Files.
Read it as a page, jumping by the outline on the left.
Press Edit to change a section, or Ask to put a question about it: the change is written to the real file.

/files.what: Every file in the brain in one table, the newest first, so any file can be opened here instead of in a program on the desktop. Press a column's name to sort by it and press it again to reverse. A file changed today is marked in the accent color, one changed this week more softly.

parts.name: The folders
parts.line: Down the left: every top-level folder with how many files it holds. Press one to show only its files; the arrow beside it opens the folders inside it.

parts.name: The types
parts.line: A row of chips above the folders: press one to show only that kind of file, press it again to show all.

parts.name: The box
parts.line: Type part of a name or a path and the table keeps only the files whose path holds it.

parts.name: A row
parts.line: Opens the file: a document, a script or a data file in the Reader, a picture in the picture viewer, a drawing in the Forge, read mode, anything else (a spreadsheet, a Word file, a PDF) as a download. The back button returns to the table as you left it.

parts.name: Last touched by
parts.line: Who last wrote a line in the brain's log naming the file, and what they did.

workflow: Find the file: the newest are on top, or type part of its name in the box.
Press a column's name to sort by it.
Press a row to open the file beside the page.

/preview.what: A web page shown inside the viewer, so a site mockup, a page design or a dev server can be looked at next to the brain without leaving it. A page from the brain reloads by itself when its file changes, and the width row shows it as a phone, a tablet or a laptop would.

parts.name: The pages
parts.line: Down the left: every web page in the brain, grouped by folder, the newest first. Press one to show it.

parts.name: The address box
parts.line: Type an address and press open: a dev server running on this computer (localhost) or a live site.

parts.name: The widths
parts.line: Full, 1280, 768 and 375: the frame takes that width and sits in the middle, so the page can be checked at laptop, tablet and phone size.

parts.name: Reload
parts.line: Loads the page again now. A page from the brain also reloads on its own within two seconds of its file changing, and says when.

parts.name: The links
parts.line: Open the source shows the page's file in the Reader; open in a new tab shows it on its own.

parts.name: A blank frame
parts.line: Some sites refuse to be shown inside another page. When the frame stays blank, open the site in a tab instead.

workflow: Pick a page from the brain, or type an address.
Switch between phone, tablet and laptop widths.
Change the file: the page reloads by itself.

/threads.what: Every piece of work that runs across the ledgers, one row each: a placement, a partnership, a launch. A piece of a larger thread sits under it, indented, and the larger thread's count includes its pieces'. Each row says who it is about, how many open items wait on you and how many are open in all, and the date of its newest dated line. Press a row to open its thread.

parts.name: A row
parts.line: The thread's name, its people, your open items and all of its open items. Press it to open the thread.

workflow: Find the piece of work: a placement, a partnership, a launch.
Read its counts: what waits on you, and what is open in all.
Press the row to open its thread.

/thread.what: One piece of work on one page, its workspace. From the top: the way back (every thread, and the thread this is a piece of), its open questions, the thing being made right now, where it stands, how it connects to other work, its pieces, what was built for it, its documents, and the rest of what needs you. Beside it: the next call, the progress so far and the people. It is read from the subject file and the ledgers each time it opens, so it is never out of date. Press an item's words to work on it here: the item, its brief, its files, its history and its note take the top of the page and the thread stays around it; back to the thread clears it. An item that belongs to no thread opens here on its own, with every block around it. An item whose answer is a choice between things to look at opens on them first, side by side, each with its answer press under it.

parts.name: The way back
parts.line: Above the name: every thread, then the thread this one is a piece of, when it is one. Each is one press.

parts.name: Share with <member>
parts.line: Under the thread's name, in a brain that shares a copy with someone and when their copy holds this thread's file: share with <member> puts the thread on the From band of their Today, under Shared with you, one press to this page in their copy, the next time it syncs. Once shared, the line says shared with <member>, with stop sharing. What they see is their copy of it: the thread's file and the items of the lists they hold, never a list that stays in your brain. Each task here carries the same press in its row.

parts.name: Questions
parts.line: This work's own open questions (the ones that link it), first on the page: the ones waiting on you first, then the ones other work waits on, then the soonest due, then the newest, a set asked on the same day in the order it was asked. A question the thread takes in only because it names its people or its words stays in What needs you, under the thread's own items. When others are asked too, yours sit under For you and theirs under Asked of others. Answer one right here; it leaves the list and the next stands in its place. With no open question, the card is not drawn and Where it stands moves up.

parts.name: In progress
parts.line: The thing being made right now for this work, framed under the questions: its name, one line on what it is, Open (a page opens itself in a new tab, a document opens in the Reader), Preview for a page, and what happens next on it.

parts.name: Where it stands
parts.line: The subject file's own summary. An item it names is a small press carrying the item's words, never a code; another thread it names is a press to that thread; the file opens in the Reader from the foot.

parts.name: How it connects
parts.line: A small drawing: this work in the middle, what it is part of above, its pieces below, what feeds it or what it feeds to the left, what sits beside it or what it builds on to the right. Each box is a press to that work, with one line on how they connect under it. Only connections the subject file records are drawn.

parts.name: Pieces of this
parts.line: The threads that are pieces of this one, each with its open items. Their items are counted here too, and an item two of them take in belongs to the piece.

parts.name: Built here
parts.line: Every page or site made for this work, by its own name, with Open (the thing itself, in a new tab), Preview (inside the viewer at phone, tablet and laptop widths) and About (the note kept beside it).

parts.name: Documents
parts.line: The rest of the work's files, by their names, newest first, each opening in the Reader.

parts.name: What needs you
parts.line: Every other open item on every ledger that belongs to this work; its own open questions are at the top of the page, and the count says how many. The ones other work waits on come first, then yours, then Claude's, then everyone else's; inside each, the items that link this work come before those that only name its people or its words, then the soonest due, then the newest. A link that names an item (from Today's In progress strip, or an item's own link) scrolls the page to it and flashes it. Answer, close, hold or leave a note right here, the same presses as the Today page. A survey carries one press, Take the survey, which opens it on a page of its own. A choice between things to look at carries one press, Compare, which opens it here on them side by side. A thread whose subject file carries the line gather: own takes in only the items on its own project's ledger and the items that link to it, so other work its people are on stays out; its people are still shown beside it, and the line under its name says it takes in only its own items and what links it.

parts.name: Next call
parts.line: The next call on the calendar with one of its people, and its prep when one is written.

parts.name: Progress
parts.line: A fold beside the page, closed until you open it; it remembers whether it is open for each thread. Inside, a column you can scroll and make taller or shorter from the handle at its foot: what is done (newest first, with what each made), what is next (press one to work on it here) and what is held for later.

parts.name: Working on
parts.line: The item you pressed, at the top: its presses, a brief that says what you need to know (Brief me writes it, Refresh writes it again), its own files, its history and a box for its note. While a question is open here, the other open questions to you on this thread stand right under it with their presses, and when you answer, the next one takes its place. Back to the thread clears it, and the browser's back button steps through the items you opened.

parts.name: A picture in a note
parts.line: A note can carry a picture. Paste one into an item's note box: it is kept in the brain and the box shows where, and once the note is written the picture is drawn under the note's words. Writing a picture's place in the brain, or a link to it, in a note does the same. A press on the picture opens it in the image viewer. A web address stays a link. In a team copy a pasted picture is not kept (a copy adds no files); a picture already in the copy can be linked.

parts.name: Compare
parts.line: An item whose answer is a choice between things to look at opens on them first, one column each, side by side on a wide window and one under the other on a narrow one: the name on top, the thing itself below it (a page or a document in a frame, a picture as itself), Full screen to open it in its own tab, a press for each screen when the page has several, and under it the press that answers with that one, which then takes you back to where you came from. An option with nothing to look at, such as none of these, is a column with its name and its press. Under the columns, a box to answer in your own words. Once answered, your answer is marked and the presses go.

parts.name: People
parts.line: Each person the thread is about, with where things stand with them.

parts.name: On a phone
parts.line: Below 600 pixels wide the header is one line: back, the page's name and menu. Menu unfolds the rest under that line (the day, the search, this page's own controls, the list of pages, with what's new first under more, and the question mark); a press anywhere else, or Escape, folds it again. While the viewer has changed and you have not pressed Seen, the menu press carries a dot.

workflow: Read where it stands and what needs you, at the top.
Press an item's words to work on it here, with its brief, its files and its history.
Look at the next call and the progress beside it before you move on.

/forge.what: One drawing of how part of the brain works, in one of three modes, switched at the top. Read shows it as drawn, and a part that names another drawing opens that drawing, with the back press walking back through them. Live shows the same drawing against what really runs: each part tied to the file, project or service it stands for, lit by what moved in the last two weeks. Edit changes it: cells with typed parts and labelled lines, saved back to the same file Obsidian reads. With no drawing named, it is the picker: the maps first, grouped by what they are for, each with how much of it moved recently (the counts fill in a moment after the page shows), then every other drawing by family, and a box to start a new one. The header's forge entry opens it; old maps links land here.

parts.name: The picker
parts.line: The maps by purpose, then the other drawings by family. Open live, read or edit on each row opens that drawing on this page.

parts.name: Read, live, edit
parts.line: The three views of the same drawing. The address carries the mode, so a link opens the view it was sent in.

parts.name: A cell
parts.line: One piece of the system: its outer band is what people see, its core is what runs.

parts.name: A part
parts.line: Typed, and able to carry the document that specifies it. In read mode a part that names a drawing or a file opens it.

parts.name: Stages
parts.line: Concept, prototype, built, stable. The colour and the weight say which.

parts.name: The Share line
parts.line: At the bottom left of an open drawing, when the brain shares files with someone: shared, or yours with Share with <owner> (the drawing's .forge.json goes with it); in the owner's brain, Send to <member> now on a drawing of a shared folder.

workflow: Pick a drawing from the picker.
Read it, or switch to live to see what really runs, each part lit by what moved.
Switch to edit to change it, and save: Obsidian opens the same file.

/mentee.what: Every mentee-facing piece of the programme in the order a mentee meets it, each one editable in place. What the stage is for, what pieces belong to it, whether each piece exists yet and when it last changed.

parts.name: A stage
parts.line: One step of the programme, with why it is there.

parts.name: A piece
parts.line: The document a mentee actually gets, openable and editable.

parts.name: Mark reviewed
parts.line: Saves the manifest back after a pass through it.

workflow: Go down the stages in the order a mentee meets them.
Open a piece to read it or change it in place.
Mark it reviewed when it is right.

/call.what: One call on one flat page, for while you are on it: the call's name and time with a press to join it, a card for everyone on it that opens their page, what is due on this call, the questions grouped as the prep writes them with a box to tick each one, the points per person, and your notes. Nothing is folded. Reached from Next on the board, or from a prep in the Reader.

parts.name: Join the call
parts.line: Opens the meeting link from the calendar in a new tab.

parts.name: The cards
parts.line: One per person on the call, with their role and where it stands; press one for their page.

parts.name: The questions
parts.line: Tick a question when it is asked. The tick is written into the prep itself, and ticked ones move to the bottom of their group.

parts.name: Your notes
parts.line: Saved into the prep's notes section when you click away from the box.

parts.name: The transcript
parts.line: Add the transcript Gemini made (the plain-text file, or drop it on the box): it is filed against this call, and the page shows what the drop step printed, who spoke and where it went. A transcript a session pulled from Gemini's email shows here too, marked pulled from Gemini. Once one is filed, run the import chain asks the session to read the call in. Once the call has ended this sits right under the call's name.

parts.name: A code in the text
parts.line: Shows the item's first words beside it; press it to open that item on Projects.

workflow: Press join when the call starts.
Tick each question as it is answered, and write your notes in the box.
After the call, add the transcript under The transcript and press run the import chain: what came out of it flows back to the cards and the threads.

/from-claude.what: What the overnight checks found and what others sent you, on one page. The findings the night's checks filed, ten to a page, with where each came from as the filter; and, only when there is something, what a team copy or another person's viewer sent you, with a press that brings an item into your folders. Nothing here is due: it waits until you look. A proposal that wants your verdict comes to Today as a question, like every other question.

parts.name: Found overnight
parts.line: Problems the checks filed on the projects, the most repeated and the oldest first, ten to a page. The chips at the top show one source at a time; the project and owner presses on a row narrow to that one.

parts.name: Sent to you
parts.line: Shown only when something arrived: what another person's viewer sent through a shared folder, and the changes a team copy proposed. In a team copy it is your inbox from the brain's owner: press pull for what is new, then bring into my folder on an item to copy it into your own folder; nothing lands there without that press.

workflow: Read what the overnight checks found, and act on what matters.
Open what was sent to you, and bring an item into your folders if you want it.
Answer a proposal where it waits: on Today, as a question with its choices.

/opportunities.what: Every opportunity the brain carries, by stage: heard of, in conversation, offered, live, and the dead ones folded at the foot. Each says who it reaches through, who it is with, what could come of it, how long since it was named and since it last moved, and the next move.

parts.name: The top lines
parts.line: How many opportunities there are at each stage, and how many of each kind.

parts.name: through and kind
parts.line: Narrow the list to the ones one person holds, or to one kind. Nothing to type.

parts.name: move to
parts.line: Press a stage on a row to move it there. The row's moved count starts again from today, and the change is written to the file with a log line.

parts.name: set next move
parts.line: Write the next move and whose it is; change or clear it later. The same goes onto the card's own opportunity line on People.

parts.name: Names
parts.line: A name with a card opens it on People. A name with no card opens the card of the person they are reached through, where they sit under Their circle.

workflow: Read the stages, from heard of to live.
Open one to see who it reaches through and how long since it moved.
Move it to its next stage, or set its next move.

/artifacts.what: Everything built in the brain, by its name: the sites, the page designs, the mockups, the newest first. A site of several pages is one row, opened at its first page. This is the place to find a website that is being made and look at it.

parts.name: The name
parts.line: What the thing is called, taken from the page's own title. Pressing it opens the page itself in a new tab.

parts.name: The line under it
parts.line: What it is, from the note kept beside it when there is one, and when it last changed. The small grey line is where its file sits, for reference only.

parts.name: open
parts.line: The page itself, full window, in a new tab, working as it would for anyone who visits it.

parts.name: preview
parts.line: The same page inside the viewer, where the width row shows it as a phone, a tablet or a laptop would, and it reloads when its file changes.

parts.name: about
parts.line: Shown when the thing has a note beside it: opens that note in the Reader, which says what it is for and how it was made.

parts.name: Its other pages
parts.line: A site's other pages, each one press that opens it in a new tab.

workflow: Find the thing by its name: the newest are on top.
Press open to see it in a new tab, or preview to look at it here.
Press about to see what it was built for.

/survey.what: A survey on a page of its own, opened by the one press a survey question carries, Take the survey. Its title and what it is for come first, then each statement as a card with a press for every answer it offers and a line for anything you want to add. A press is saved into the survey's own file at once, and a line when you leave its box, so you can stop and come back. Finish closes the question that opened it, saying how many you answered, and goes back to Today.

parts.name: The statements
parts.line: One card each, numbered as the survey numbers them: the statement, then one press per answer it offers (agree, partly or no in most). The press you chose is filled in; press another to change it. A statement with no presses is answered in your own words, in its line.

parts.name: Your line
parts.line: The box under each statement takes one line of your own. It is saved when you leave the box or press Enter.

parts.name: Answered so far
parts.line: How many statements have an answer, at the top and again beside Finish. A statement left blank keeps the default the survey names under its introduction.

parts.name: Finish
parts.line: Answers the question on Today that opened the survey, saying how many statements you answered and that the answers are in the survey's file, then takes you back to Today. Every answer is already saved before you press it.

parts.name: The file in the Reader
parts.line: The survey's own file, where each answer sits on its statement's Answer line. The Reader shows the same lines.

workflow: Read what the survey is for, at the top.
Press an answer on each statement, adding a line where you want.
Press Finish: the question that opened it closes.

/usage.what: Which prompts and actions used the most of the plan, today and over the last seven days, so what drains it can be seen and changed. A turn is one prompt with everything it set off, its workers included. The figures are in API $ equivalent, a proxy for plan usage: the plan publishes no figure per prompt, so each reply is priced at the API's list price for its model, and writing to the cache at one and a quarter to two times the input price. Read from the Claude Code sessions on this computer only.

parts.name: The week
parts.line: Seven bars, one a day, the picked day dark and today named under its date. Press a day to see its turns. Under the bars, the week's total split by who started the turns.

parts.name: Top turns
parts.line: The ten turns of the picked day that cost the most, then the ten of the whole week. Each shows its cost, its time, who started it, its first words (a background task, a scheduled run or a command by its name), its session, the models, the split and why it cost that.

parts.name: Who started it
parts.line: you: a prompt you sent. background wake: a background task or a watcher finished and woke the session. another session: a worker's report or a message from another session. session brief: the brief a session was started with. scheduled: a scheduled run. app event: a notice from the app.

parts.name: The split
parts.line: The small bar: the session's own share of the cost and its workers' (subagents'), the workers' percentage beside it. A worker's cost belongs to the turn that sent it.

parts.name: Why
parts.line: The line under a turn says where most of its cost went: its workers, writing its context to the cache, re-reading its context call after call, its output, or new input.

parts.name: Sessions this week
parts.line: Every session of the week, the most first, with its turn count and what it cost on the picked day. Press one to open its turns of that day in order: the time, the cost, the calls, the context size, who started it and how long the session sat idle before. Pressing a session's name on any turn opens the same.

parts.name: Why an idle wake costs what it does
parts.line: A session keeps its context in a cache that lives five minutes or an hour. The first turn after a longer pause writes the whole context to the cache again, at one and a quarter to two times the input price, before it does anything else. A long session carries a big context, so a short answer late in it, or a watcher waking it after an hour, can cost as much as a working turn.

parts.name: What the figures are not
parts.line: The plan's own meter: its percentages for the five hours and the week are not on this page. Each figure here is what the same tokens would cost at the API's list price.

parts.name: On a phone
parts.line: Below 600 pixels wide the header is one line: back, the page's name and menu. Menu unfolds the rest under that line (the day, the search, this page's own controls, the list of pages, with what's new first under more, and the question mark); a press anywhere else, or Escape, folds it again. While the viewer has changed and you have not pressed Seen, the menu press carries a dot.

workflow: Look at the week's bars for the expensive days.
Read a day's top turns: what started each one, and why it cost that.
Change what drains the plan: a habit, a schedule, a model.

/share.what: One person's copy of the brain as a checklist: everything the sharing tiers send to that copy, each with a tick, so you can hold back what should not go before the next send. Opens folded, each band with its count.

parts.name: Folders and files that go
parts.line: Each shared folder with how many of its files go; open it for the files. Untick a folder or a file to hold it back from this copy only, and say why in a line if you want. It stays out from the next send.

parts.name: People cards
parts.line: Every card, ticked when it goes. Untick one to hold it back from every copy; tick a held one to send it. Open a card's sections to keep one part out: that section is marked [private] on its heading in the card, and every copy leaves it out.

parts.name: Not shared
parts.line: The folders the sharing tiers keep private. Their tier is changed in the brain's registry, never with a tick here.

parts.name: Never crosses
parts.line: The root files, the code except the tools a copy runs, and any person marked never crosses. Nothing here has a tick.

workflow: Pick the person whose copy you are checking.
Untick what should not go, or a part of a people card.
Leave it: the next nightly send follows the ticks.

/settings.what: What you can change in the viewer, saved at once in your settings file. The first group is how your answers reach the main agent; the second shows the Studio's connections.

parts.name: Sending your answers
parts.line: On by default: an answer, done, hold or note is saved the moment you press it, and goes to the main agent when you press Send at the bottom right of any page, when you leave the viewer (another tab, the window closed, the phone locked), or after the minutes you set here with no new press. Moving from one viewer page to another does not send. Turn it off and each press goes the moment you make it.

parts.name: The Send press
parts.line: At the bottom right of every page while answers are held. It reads Send and the number waiting; with nothing waiting it is a faint round press. Hover or focus it to see when they go on their own.

parts.name: The Studio's connections
parts.line: Which image providers are ready and, for the local one, the ComfyUI address, its folder, the four model files and the time one picture may take, each with the setting in your settings file that changes it. Read only here.

workflow: Read each setting and what it does.
Change it: it is saved at once.
Go back to the page you were on: the change holds from your next press.

/manual.what: The manual of the brain and the viewer, put together when you open it from the files that explain each part: every page's card, every folder's and every module's readme, the definition of the viewer and its rules. Sixteen chapters in the order of a day; each has For you, what a part is and how you use it, and Under the hood, the readmes, folded. Every section ends with the file it came from and the day that file last changed, and a readme that does not name a newer file in its folder says so. What you changed, at the top, lists what is yours beside what the viewer ships: your notes on a section, the settings you changed, your board, the widgets and looks you wrote and their readmes. The "?" on any page opens that page's card, with one press from there to its chapter here.
workflow: Open a chapter from the contents, or press the "?" on any page and then the press to its chapter.
Read For you; open Under the hood when you want to know how it is built.
Add a note of your own to a section: What you changed lists every note, setting and module of yours.

parts.name: Contents
parts.line: Down the left, the chapters in order, each with a mark when you wrote a note in it or one of its readmes is behind its folder. On a phone it folds to one line at the top.

parts.name: What you changed
parts.line: One line at the top that opens the list, chapter by chapter: your notes, the settings that differ from what the viewer ships, your board, your looks and widgets with their readmes. With nothing of yours it says so.

parts.name: For you
parts.line: Each page's card as the "?" shows it, with a typical workflow in three steps and its parts one press away; an instrument's card; the parts of the definition that say what the viewer is for.

parts.name: Under the hood
parts.line: One fold per readme or document, closed. Opening it reads the file as it is now.

parts.name: The line under a section
parts.line: The file it came from, by its title (press it to open the file beside the page), and the day it last changed. A readme that does not name a newer file in its folder says which one.

parts.name: Your note
parts.line: Under any chapter or section: press add a note, write it, and press keep. It is kept in your own folder, which an update never touches; empty it to take it away.

parts.name: Not in a chapter yet
parts.line: A folder, page or module with no chapter is listed at the end rather than left out, and the rounds fail until it is given one.

glossary._about: Every word the app uses, with a definition, an example and, where there is one, the Septabee analog. Served at GET /api/glossary and rendered at /glossary; every term is underlined wherever it appears, with its definition on hover (the everyday words only where a writer marks them). A group's pages say which group the glossary opens for the page the ? panel was pressed on. Moved here from brain-viewer-holon/brain-viewer-glossary.md on 2026-10-16, with the ledger's kinds and tags added (The things on a ledger) and the entries on where an item is acted on and what the ? button opens corrected.
glossary.keys_note: While the cursor is in anything you type into (the notepad, a message, a reply, an answer, a Forge name, the manual's search), no key below does its page job; Escape leaves the box first, then works as listed. Every key the app already answers to. No key is hidden: the ones that apply on the page you are looking at are named in the bottom-right corner of that page.

terms.definition: Any single thing drawn on a canvas: a box, a ring, a dot. The most general word. A node has no promise about what it does.
terms.example: every bubble on [the map](/map).

terms.definition: A node that does a job and has settings. You can swap one module for another that does the same job differently.
terms.example: the transcript processor is a module; so is the call-prep generator.

terms.definition: One of the base parts every brain gets, each with a spec, a writer, a checker and an adapter; the components doc froze this word in July and rules out calling one a module. Rule of thumb: components are the organs every brain is born with, modules are the tools you add.
terms.example: the transcript artery, the people-card system.

terms.definition: A typed piece inside a cell: a screen, form, dashboard or message on the band; a step, hook, ferryman, schedule or gate in the core; a mind, a store, or something outside. A part is a node with a type, and the palette on the right of the Forge is the list of them. (A cell's **output** is not one: it is a section of the cell's own shell.)
terms.example: in the onboarding cell canvas, "Script · Autopopulate" is a part.

terms.definition: A boundary the brain calls across, drawn as one part: an API, an export, a scheduled hook. **On a drawing it is one symbol and nothing else** — the gate — with its counts underneath: how many routes the other side has, how many the token the brain holds may call, how many nothing in the brain calls yet. A small clock on it means the inventory it was drawn from is more than a week old. **Double-clicking it opens its [adapter sheet](#adapter-sheet)**, the second view, in a page of its own. Which adapters exist is a file, `skills/brain-viewer/adapters.json`, so an `**Adapter · <name>**` head on any canvas binds to the same boundary by name. Nothing of the second view is stored in the drawing; it is computed from the other system's own catalog every time the page asks, so it cannot go stale the way a hand-drawn map does. `Ferryman` is the same word (it keeps the boat symbol).
terms.example: the Ferryman on [the Ferryman map](/live?path=projects%2Fpf-build%2Farchitecture%2Fdata-flow%2Fferryman-map.canvas), 71 ports, and its written twin at [[pf-app-holon/pf-app-adapter-ferryman.md]].

terms.definition: The second view of an adapter, in a place of its own: `/forge?adapter=<name>`, opened by double-clicking the adapter on any drawing. Three columns, all generated and read-only — on the left the skills that call the boundary, one named box each; down the middle the adapter with one **port** per route, grouped by resource and, inside a group, by who may call it; on the right the other system's stores, one named box per resource group — with a short straight **cable** from each port to what calls it and to what it reaches. It exists because the same thing drawn on top of a hand-drawn map was unreadable: the names were hidden, the boxes were blank and the cables landed on the title block. Nothing hand-drawn competes with it, and nothing on it is written to any canvas. **back** returns to the drawing you came from.
terms.example: [the Ferryman's sheet](/forge?adapter=ferryman).

terms.definition: Two things, one word, and the drawing tells them apart by what you are looking at. **On an adapter:** one route on the other side of the boundary — a method and a path — drawn as a dot, in a group per resource. **Solid** means the token the brain holds may call it, **dim** means it needs the admin key, **hollow** means the route exists in the app and nothing in the brain calls it (built, not yet wired), and **red** means a skill calls a path the app's catalog has never listed. A red ring around it means a probe came back 4xx or 5xx, and a **dotted** edge means it is a [manual port](#manual-port). Hover for the method and the path, press it for its card: the purpose, who may call it, every caller as a `file:line` you can open, when the resource last ran, whether the brain keeps a mirror, and the health code. **On a part, a cell or a blob:** the four points on its rim that appear under the pointer, where a line can start or end.
terms.example: `POST /api/v1/transcripts/import` on the Ferryman, solid, called by `skills/ferryman/push.py`; and dragging from one on the onboarding app cell's rim to draw a line.

terms.definition: The ports of one resource, kept together: every `/contacts` route in one band, every `/transcripts` route in the next, each with the store it reaches on the app side. Inside a group the ports are ordered by **tier** — the ones the personal token may call first, the ones needing the admin key next, the ones nothing in the brain calls last — so what is wired and what is not read as two halves rather than a shuffle. When an adapter sits inside a cell, the whole thing shrinks to three counted arcs on its rim in those same three tiers. Most groups are read from the catalog; a group can also be added by hand — see **manual port**.
terms.example: *transcripts* on the Ferryman, nine routes, mirrored at `pf-app-holon/transcripts/`.

terms.definition: A port written by hand in `skills/brain-viewer/adapters.json` rather than read from the other system's catalog, for a boundary that does not describe itself. It is merged into its resource group like any other port and drawn with a **dotted** edge everywhere, because it is a claim a person made and not the app's own word. Its callers are named in the registry too. When the system does grow a catalog, the hand-written group is replaced and the dots go away.
terms.example: the five `/candidates` calls on [the onboarding pull](/forge?adapter=onboarding), which has no self-description to read.

terms.definition: A line on an [adapter sheet](#adapter-sheet), drawn rather than typed: from a port to what calls it on the brain side, and from that port to the store it reaches in the outside system; and, when an adapter sits inside a cell, from its arcs to the parts of that cell that call it. **The arrowhead is the direction the call pushes:** a GET points toward the brain, a POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE points toward the app. A cable to a port nothing calls is dashed and faint, a cable from a drift row is red, and a cable to a manual port is dotted. Hover one for its plain name, the first clause of the route's purpose. It is a **line** seen at the adapter level: a line is drawn by hand and saved in the canvas, a cable is generated and saved nowhere.
terms.example: `skills/call-prep` to `GET /api/v1/contacts` to the contacts store.

terms.definition: Retired 2026-09-18. It used to mean one cable standing for a whole resource group while the whole drawing was on screen, with the group's ports collapsed behind a count — the way an adapter fanned out onto the map it sat on. Nothing fans out onto a map any more: a drawing shows the adapter as one symbol with its counts, the detail moved to the **adapter sheet**, and the compact form inside a cell is three counted arcs, one per **port group** tier. The word is kept here only so an older note that uses it can be read.
Information moving from one node to another, in a direction, labelled with what moves.
terms.example: "pull the application" between the website cell and the app cell.

terms.definition: A node drawn as a circle standing for one thing you can open: a conversation, a session, a sub-agent, a project, a person. A ring band, the thing's own glyph in the middle, its name under it, a count on the corner when it has one, and a gold ring while it is running; double-click one for what is inside it. The gold dot travelling along a line is an **in-flight bubble** (below) and is the only other thing the word covers.
terms.example: every conversation and session on [the agents page](/agents), and the small ones in Running now on [the home page](/).

terms.definition: A store drawn against the OUTSIDE of a cell's wall: a round shape touching the rim, where what the cell keeps sits beside the mouth. It slides to a free stretch of rim so it never covers a name, it carries a pointer to the real table, file or page behind it, and a double-click opens that beside the drawing. Far out it draws the store's own symbol where its name would be. A blob is a **store** seen from outside the wall; the same store drawn inside the core is the green box.
terms.example: the profiles store at the wall of [the onboarding app cell](/forge?path=projects/pf-build/architecture/womb-phase/onboarding-app-cells.canvas).

terms.definition: A container that holds parts and sets how they behave; the outside band is what people see (UI), the inside is what runs.
terms.example: the onboarding app drawn as a cell.

terms.definition: The one section of a cell's shell that what it makes leaves through: a segment on the outside of its wall, in its own color, which slides around the ring so it can face whatever comes next. Double-click it for its shelf: the loose fields the cell makes and the packages already named. It replaced the old core part called *assumed output* on 2026-09-10, so there is one word for this and one place it is drawn.
terms.example: the mouth on [the onboarding app cell](/forge?path=projects/pf-build/architecture/womb-phase/onboarding-app-cells.canvas), facing the interview.

terms.definition: One thing a cell makes, by the name the real record gives it: an email address, a location, an archetype. Where the cell is bound to something real the fields are read from that thing's own records rather than typed, so a schema that gains a key gains a field.
terms.example: `email` and `profile.whyProspectforge`, read from the onboarding app's candidate records.

terms.definition: Fields picked and named together because they travel as one thing: a form, a card, a packet. A package sits as a tile **on** the ring, its inner edge flush against the mouth, and dragging it onto another cell draws the line from the tile, labelled with its name and nothing else. It is one of the few things still drawn with the whole drawing on screen, because seeing what is packed is the point.
terms.example: *the application form* on the onboarding app cell, eleven fields, shipped to the brain as a people card.

terms.definition: One filled package on its way: the fields of a package with a single record's values in them, travelling down a line as one thing. The **package** is the shape (which fields go together, under one name); the packet is one of them actually going, and it is what the gold dot on a line stands for.
terms.example: one candidate's application form arriving at the interview cell — the *application form* package, with that candidate's eleven answers in it.

terms.definition: A folder in the brain that declares what it is and what lives in it, which agent runs inside it, its rules and its status. Holons hold other holons.
terms.example: the PF company folder, [[brain-viewer-holon/readme.md|the Brain Viewer holon]], the PF App holon. A cell is a holon drawn; a holon is a cell stored.

terms.definition: The page where a system is designed before it exists: cells, typed parts and labelled lines drawn on a canvas, with a palette of part types on the right, an inspector for the selected thing, undo, and an explicit save back to the same canvas file Obsidian reads.
terms.example: [the onboarding pipeline opened in the Forge](/forge?path=projects/pf-build/architecture/womb-phase/onboarding-app-cells.canvas); the picker of every drawing at [/forge](/forge).

groups.name: The things that move and decide

terms.definition: A rule or a small skill that fires when something happens and decides what to do next.
terms.example: the dispatcher's rules over the log; the log-integrity check that runs at the end of every turn.

terms.definition: The main agent's line of thought: the chat the owner talks to, and everything that rides along it.
terms.example: the Main chat on [the home page](/).

terms.definition: Handing a job from the primary current to a holon's agent and getting a shaped result back.
terms.example: the main chat farming research out to a scout.

terms.definition: The brain's transcoder between the brain and an app: it reads one shape and delivers another. It is an **adapter** (the same part type, drawn with the boat), so on a drawing it carries the generated port level.
terms.example: the push that carries a transcript's summary into the PF App.

terms.definition: A model with instructions and a scope, running inside a holon.
terms.example: the Brain Viewer agent, the PF App agent, a scout.

terms.definition: An agent another agent started for one job, with its own model and instructions, which reports back and then ends. Drawn as a smaller bubble attached to the one that started it.
terms.example: the opus workers a project agent sends off, under their conversation on [the agents page](/agents).

terms.definition: One continuous line of talk with an agent: the same agent, holding the same memory, picked up again every time you send. The app keeps it as a Claude Code session and resumes that session, so a conversation and a session are two words for the same thing seen from either end.
terms.example: any row in the list on the left of [the home page](/).

terms.definition: Handing one agent's answer to another: the quoted reply plus your note become the next message in that agent's conversation, and the line between the two is kept so the drawing can show it. Started by the control under an answer, or by dragging one bubble onto another.
terms.example: an answer from a project agent handed to Main to be checked.
