groups.name: The things that record and organize

terms.definition: One file per project holding its tasks and questions, one per line, with an owner and dates. Listed by milestone on [the Projects panel](/projects); answered, closed or put off on Today and on the item's thread page.
terms.example: [[brain-viewer-holon/brain-viewer-tasks.md|this holon's own ledger]].

terms.definition: The build order drawn as one horizontal line, a dot per step, filled once a step closes, with the step the build is on marked and named; hover or click a dot for its name and, once it is done, a link to what it built. It reads the Straight-line milestone off the ledgers, so it is the ledger seen sideways rather than a second copy of it.
terms.example: the nine dots above [Waiting on you on the home page](/), and the same line above the milestones on [the Brain Viewer ledger](/projects?id=brain-viewer-holon).

terms.definition: A line you write back on a task instead of ticking it: it is saved as that item's note, dated, and the item stays open. The box sits under every task of yours on Today and on the task's thread page; a box ticked with words still in it writes both. A picture pasted into the box, or linked in the words, is drawn under the note.
terms.example: the note box under a task in Yours to do on [Today](/).

terms.definition: The box in the bottom-left corner of every page, folded to one line until you open it: somewhere to write a note the moment you have it, with a picture pasted or attached to it. Saving writes one dated markdown file into `thoughts/notepad/` with the picture beside it, and the note is then a real brain file: it opens in the Reader and its path can be dropped into a message or onto a ledger item.
terms.example: the notepad tab at the bottom left of [the Projects panel](/projects).

terms.definition: One screen of the app (the word *page* means the same thing).
terms.example: People, Projects, Chat, Map, Canvases.

terms.definition: A hand-drawn diagram (Obsidian format) the app renders; the intent layer of a machine.
terms.example: the data-flow map, the onboarding cells, on [the Canvases panel](/canvases).

terms.definition: The list of holons and what each declares.
terms.example: [[context/holon-registry.json]].

terms.definition: The append-only record of every agent action, the event stream the dispatcher reads.
terms.example: [[context/log.md]].

terms.definition: A ledger question that points at one part of a document: the portion you must strike, reorder or decide, with a link that opens the Reader at that section, so the document stays whole. Answered on Today or the item's thread page; the Projects panel lists it.
terms.example: [the build doc's undecided list, section 7](/reader?path=brain-viewer-holon/brain-viewer-build-doc.md#7-undecided-the-conversation), asked from the viewer's ledger; the ask button sits on every section header.

terms.definition: The blocks in a brain file written for whoever reads it next rather than for you: the banners in quotes at the top, a previous header kept under a comment, the `**STATUS:` lines, and anything a writer marks `<!-- agent -->`. The Reader keeps them off the front of a document and puts them back exactly where they sit in the file when you press *show agent notes*, dimmed and each one tagged *agent*.
terms.example: the rule banner at the top of [the pricing file](/reader?path=projects/pf-build/pf-pricing.md).

terms.definition: Every dated block in a document: a previous header, a superseded section, a dated priority stack, the folds on a person's card. A heading that starts with a date, or carries *previous*, *superseded*, *history* or *Cold storage*, puts its whole section on the back; *history* in the Reader turns to it and *front* returns. A date in parentheses is provenance and leaves the heading on the front, and a file that is nothing but dated blocks keeps them all on its front.
terms.example: the dated folds on a long-running mentee's card, opened in the Reader from [the people list](/people).

terms.definition: The page that opens a brain document organized by its headings, with strike and reorder on every list item, saved back to the file and logged.
terms.example: [the build doc opened at section 8](/reader?path=brain-viewer-holon/brain-viewer-build-doc.md#8-possible-next-moves-for-him-to-strike-or-reorder-nothing-starts-until-he-says). Lives at `/reader?path=<file>#<heading>`; the *reader* link sits at the right of every top bar.

terms.definition: The one status a people card carries: a single line under the person's name, dated, saying where they stand today. Rewritten in place whenever it changes, never appended to, and every clause in it traces to something already on the card. It is what the People page shows first and what an agent reads before answering any question about that person.
terms.example: the dated line on the card of a mentee who dropped out, which says so and where the seat went; every card is at [/people](/people).

terms.definition: What you get on click: the Where-it-stands line and its date, what is open for you about them, when you last spoke and how often, the next call, what they are building, how to reach them. The page composes it from the card's standard sections plus what it can compute, so nothing on the front is typed twice.
terms.example: the top of a mentor's card at [/people](/people).

terms.definition: Everything the front was written from, behind one fold: the dated folds, the flags and watchouts, the pipeline detail, the notes, and any status section the card carried before the format changed. Kept, never deleted, and never current unless the front says it is.
terms.example: the *History* fold on a long-running mentee's card at [/people](/people), twenty sections.

terms.definition: A card whose status has stopped without anyone noticing: no Where-it-stands line at all, a line more than thirty days old, or a dated `[status]` fold newer than the line. Marked on the card and on the row in the list, and reported by the brain's lint as check L12.
terms.example: the mark on every card not yet moved to the new format, in the list at [/people](/people).

terms.definition: A question the work cannot move past: an open task on the same ledger is marked as waiting on that question, so it stays stopped until the question is answered. A blocking question comes first in its group of Yours to do on [Today](/), naming the task it blocks, and wears a **blocking** badge on [the Projects panel](/projects). It is not *on hold*: on hold is work you put down yourself, blocking is work somebody else is waiting on.
terms.example: the open question about where call preps and their notes go after a call, with the task that files them waiting behind it.

terms.definition: A task of yours you are not doing now and have not finished: it carries the day it comes back, and until then it leaves Yours to do on Today, the project pages, the people pages and the thread pages. It is still open and still owed: nothing about it is closed, and nobody else is waiting on it, which is what makes it different from blocked. The **hold** press beside a task on Today or its thread page puts it down for three days; the small date box beside that press picks another day; **bring back** returns it early. Today keeps the held tasks folded under one *On hold* line with their count.
terms.example: a test item you would rather look at next week.

terms.definition: A member's own brain that holds the files the owner shares with her, both of them working on the same files. A file that came from the owner is shared: she edits it in place and the change goes to him, laid onto his own file so the lines of his she never saw stay; his changes come to her the same way. A file she makes is hers until she presses Share. When both changed the same lines before a sync, the owner's version stays and hers goes to him to decide. It syncs when someone works: a moment after a save, at start, and on sync now; never on a timer.
terms.example: the strip under the header of every page in her brain, Your brain, sharing with <owner>, with sync now.

groups.name: The things on a ledger
groups.note: What a project's list of work is made of, and the shapes the pages draw them in. The rules an agent files by are the ledger tool's readme, under Projects in the manual; this is the same vocabulary for a person reading the page.

terms.definition: Something one person owes: you, Claude, or a contact with a card. It is open, done, blocked on a question, or on hold until a day. On Today a task of yours has the done press, the hold press with its date box, and the reply press.
terms.example: a task under Yours to do on [Today](/).

terms.definition: What you do to finish a task, each a short line with the place to go, drawn under the task's words as a numbered list with a tick box each, before the chips and the note. The box is the only tick: the words never tick, a link in them opens its place, and a step that names a place carries an open press at its right that opens the same place. A tick is written to the ledger at once and reaches the session like any press, with an undo for the rest of the day; once every step is ticked, done is the card's lead press. The note sits under the steps, folded to its first line when it is long. Twelve steps at most; the history stays in the note, the reasoning in the linked file.
terms.example: a task with its steps under Up first on [Today](/).

terms.definition: The exchange on an item: what you wrote with the reply press (or answered, or marked done) and what the session wrote back when it took that in, drawn under the item's note as a list of pairs, you then Claude, each with its time. The latest is open and the earlier ones fold behind one press. The reply press leaves the item as it is; a step tick or a hold draws nothing here.
terms.example: under the note on a task you replied on yesterday, on [Today](/) or on its thread page.

terms.definition: Something one party asks the other. A plain question answers Yes or No, or in your own words; once answered it closes, and any task waiting on it is released.
terms.example: a question under Yours to do on [Today](/).

terms.definition: A question that names its choices: one press per choice, drawn from the choices the asker wrote. Today's *Show* filter *decisions* lists these, and within each group of Yours to do the rows rotate task, question, decision so no kind sits in a block.
terms.example: a question with Friday, Monday and neither as its presses.

terms.definition: A question whose choices are pictures: each choice names an image in the brain, or the question links one image per choice. The presses are the pictures themselves, with the choice's words under each.
terms.example: a choice between two drafts of a card, drawn as the two cards.

terms.definition: A question answered on a page of its own, many statements at once. It carries one press, *Take the survey*, which opens the survey page; Finish there answers the question.
terms.example: [the survey page](/survey) opened from a survey question on Today.

terms.definition: A question answered by choosing between things to look at: design directions, versions of a page, pictures. It leads with one press, *Compare*, which opens its workspace on the options side by side, each with its answer press under it; the answer records the option's name.
terms.example: a choice between two header directions opened side by side on the thread page.

terms.definition: A task that was a click-through for you to try something built. None is filed any more, and the last ones were closed in October 2026: how to try a finished piece is written on the what's-new page instead, and a test opened by its own link still shows at the top of Today with a line saying what it is.
terms.example: an entry on the what's-new page, under Worth trying once.

terms.definition: Something Claude wants your verdict on. It comes to Today as a question with its choices and is answered there like every other question; until October 2026 it was a card rated good, off or wrong on the from-Claude page.
terms.example: a question on [Today](/) whose choices are the verdicts.

terms.definition: An item meant for one person's next call. It leaves Today, which says how many are waiting in preps, and arrives in that person's next call prep under Context, where it is closed once a transcript shows it was raised.
terms.example: a question for a mentor that waits in the prep for your next call with them, not on Today.

terms.definition: A label on an idea kept for a later phase: owed by nobody on any day, listed wherever its ledger is listed, and nothing more. Not a hold, which has a day it comes back.
terms.example: a viewer idea marked future on [the Projects panel](/projects).

terms.definition: A plain label from the ledger's first days, kept on the lines that carry it; the viewer does nothing with it. To put a task off, hold it.
terms.example: an early design task marked later.

terms.definition: The small *from:* line under an item: who filed it, a session, a check that runs on its own, a transcript's intake, or you. It is for the agent that will look for its own items again; it tells you nothing about the item.
terms.example: *from: import-checkup* under a task that came out of a call.

terms.definition: A card on Today that is not a ledger item: something in the brain's own output that resembles one you reacted to before, the moment quoted, then the pattern it resembles with its rule. Press *Annoying* or *Not annoying*, or write a comment; the answer goes into the record of how you work.
terms.example: the *Might annoy you* band on [Today](/), drawn only when a card is open.

terms.definition: A row on Today that is not a ledger item: one call whose action items wait for approval in the ProspectForge app. Approve all, skip until tomorrow, or open the items one by one; every press writes to the app.
terms.example: a row under Yours to do on [Today](/) after a call lands.

terms.definition: The press beside a task of yours on Today and on its thread page: puts the task down for three days (or a date you pick) and takes it out of the lists until it comes back, still open.
terms.example: a test you cannot run until the next call.

terms.definition: What should exist: the drawing itself, cells and parts and lines (build doc, section 12).
terms.example: the onboarding cells canvas as drawn, before anything was bound to it.

terms.definition: The same drawing with every part bound to a real thing: a file, a skill, an agent, a table, an endpoint.
terms.example: that canvas with "Script · Autopopulate" pointing at the script that actually runs.

terms.definition: The same drawing lit by what actually happened: log lines, transcripts, pushes, chats; the gold bubbles moving.
terms.example: the same canvas showing which parts fired today.

terms.definition: Binah is the candidate name.
terms.example: [[brain-viewer-holon/brain-viewer-build-doc.md|the build doc]], section 11.

terms.definition: How far along a cell is, one of four: concept (drawn only), prototype (some parts exist, not all real), built (every part bound to something real), stable (built and trusted). Set in the Forge's inspector, shown as a badge on the cell, stored beside the drawing in its .forge.json; a drawing with no such file has every cell at concept.
terms.example: the onboarding app cell marked prototype while the website cell stays at concept.

terms.definition: The real thing a node on a drawing stands for: a file, a canvas, a holon, a skill, an agent, a page of this app, or an outside service. Worked out from the node's own words (its wikilink or path first, then a holon or skill or agent named on its title line, then a page or a service), never stored until you press save bindings, when it is written beside the drawing in its .forge.json so the drawing carries it forward. A node bound to nothing is a concept.
terms.example: on [the data-flow map, live](/live?path=projects%2Fpf-build%2Farchitecture%2Fdata-flow%2Fpf-data-flow-map.canvas), Ferryman PULL is bound to the ferryman skill and INDEX.md to the file itself.

terms.definition: How a drawing reads with the whole of it on screen: every part is the symbol printed beside its word in this glossary and nothing else, a store is that symbol inside its blob, and a band part is the symbol already on its segment. A cell keeps its title and its stage badge, and a package keeps its name, because those are what tell you where you are and what is being shipped. Rest the pointer on a part and it says its own name again; past 60% every word is drawn.
terms.example: the onboarding drawing at the zoom that fits it on screen, where ten parts read as ten symbols. The corner readout says which of the two you are looking at.

terms.definition: An existing canvas read against real state: the same drawing the Forge edits, read-only, with the build layer (what each node is bound to) and the runtime layer (what the log recorded about it in the last fourteen days, a gold bubble on every line active today) over the intent. Several of them, one per canvas, picked by purpose.
terms.example: [the maps page](/maps) and its five groups: information flow, apps and services, the OS, machines, the daily workflow.

terms.definition: One matter worked through with people over several calls, with its own page: who it is about, where it stands, every open item on any project that concerns it, the next call and its prep, and what has been decided. Each thread is one subject file under a project's `subjects/` folder. Not a conversation in the chat, and not a standing call series (the Friday call is a series). A thread takes in every open item that names one of its people or carries one of its words; when its subject file says gather: own, it takes in only its own project's items and the items that link to it.
terms.example: a partnership worked out with a partner company's president over several calls; every thread at [/threads](/threads).

terms.definition: One item opened with everything around it: the item and its presses, its brief, its files, the people it concerns, its history and a box for notes. It is drawn inside the item's thread page, focused on that item; an item on no thread opens on a thread page of its own.
terms.example: press the words of any item on [a thread page](/threads).

terms.definition: A short write-up of one item, made on request by a model that reads the item, its thread, its files and its people and changes nothing: what it is, where it stands, what is in the way. Made with *Brief me* in the item's workspace and kept under `deliverables/briefs/`.
terms.example: the *Brief* block in any item's workspace.

terms.definition: The page that makes pictures: a prompt, the things to leave out, a provider and a model, then the run as a grid to star, edit or attach to a task. A provider whose last call was refused for money or rate shows as not ready until a run works.
terms.example: [the studio](/studio).

terms.definition: The page that shows a web page inside the viewer at phone, tablet, laptop or full width: any page in the brain, reloaded when its file changes, or an address.
terms.example: [preview](/preview).

terms.definition: The owner's word for snipping a shaped set of blocks, rules and data off as a standalone brain that keeps one thread back to the parent: it is built inside this brain first, given shape and a week of data, then cut loose to run on its own, with its checks still reaching the owner.
terms.example: a mentee's first week of a placement, shaped here and then budded off as their own brain.

groups.name: The parts you can drop in
groups.note: The picker from build doc section 14, one line each. These are reference entries: they name what a part *is* when you drop it into a cell, so they are not auto-underlined in ordinary prose; the words are too everyday. Groups: containers, people-facing (the cell's outer band), running parts (its core), minds, stores, outside, flow. The flow group also holds the **Adapter** — a boundary the brain calls across, defined with the things on a canvas above, because what it is worth knowing about it is the second view it opens. `Ferryman` is that same type under its own name and keeps the boat symbol.

terms.definition: A people-facing part: something a person looks at inside a cell. Carries who sees it and what it hands inward.
terms.example: the onboarding app's application form screen. Draws as an arc segment on the cell's outer band.

terms.definition: A screen that collects: fields in, one record out.
terms.example: the intake application. Draws as an arc segment, gold-tinted.

terms.definition: A screen that only shows: no writing, a read of state.
terms.example: the mentee content dashboard at `/mentee`.

terms.definition: A people-facing part that leaves the cell to reach a person: an email, a text, an app notification.
terms.example: the check-in nudge.

terms.definition: A running part in the cell's core: one job, deterministic, no model.
terms.example: `skills/brain-log/log.py` appending a line.

terms.definition: A running part that fires on a clock rather than on an event.
terms.example: the nightly qmd re-index.

terms.definition: A running part that waits for an approval, from a person or a rule, before the flow continues.
terms.example: the owner approving a placement; propose mode's request queue.

terms.definition: A packaged procedure an agent can call, with its own instructions.
terms.example: `skills/call-prep/`. A mind-type part.

terms.definition: The instructions a mind runs with, stored as a part so it can be read and changed.
terms.example: `skills/brain-viewer/chat-prompts/main.md`.

terms.definition: A file or a table a cell writes to and reads from.
terms.example: `context/chats/`. Draws as a green box inside the cell, or, dragged against the cell wall, as a round blob touching the rim from outside — where what is kept sits beside the mouth. A blob takes a **free stretch of the rim**: it starts beside the mouth (or at the angle you dropped it) and slides to the nearest stretch clear of the band names, the packages and the lines, so it never sits on top of a name. A blob carries a pointer to the real table, file or page, and a double-click opens it beside the drawing; that view closes on Escape, on its close button, or on a press anywhere on the drawing. Far out, the blob draws the store’s own symbol where its name would be, and the name comes back with the pointer on it. Example: the profiles store at the wall of [the onboarding app cell](/forge?path=projects/pf-build/architecture/womb-phase/onboarding-app-cells.canvas).

terms.definition: A store whose whole job is listing what exists, for something else to read.
terms.example: `pf-app-holon/pf-app-api-catalog.json`.

terms.definition: An outside system with its own users and database that a cell talks to.
terms.example: the PF App, the onboarding app. Draws as a hexagon at the cell's edge.

terms.definition: An outside system with no users of ours: an API we call.
terms.example: GitHub, Google Calendar.

terms.definition: A named human in the flow, drawn because the machine waits on them.
terms.example: a team member accepts, the owner decides.

terms.definition: A gold dot moving along a line: one message, file, record or event actually travelling right now.
terms.example: a chat turn arriving on the map.

keys.what: closes whatever is open on top: the read drawer, the image viewer, a live map's text drawer, the sheet that hands an answer to another agent.
sends the message you are typing.
a new line inside the message instead of sending it.
jumps to that page's search box.
fits the whole drawing back on screen, on the Forge and on a live map.
on a live map, turn the intent, build and runtime layers on and off; any of the three can be on at once, and the page remembers the choice.
turns the canvas grid on and off.
saves the note you are writing without reaching for the button.

opens this page's help panel: what the page is and what each part of it does, in plain words; in its top row, one press to this page's card in the manual, the whole book behind it; every word the app uses is one press further in, from the link at the panel's foot: the manual's chapter The words the viewer uses, opened in a small window meant to stay beside your work.

grow or shrink what is selected; hold S and drag a selected thing away from its middle to grow it, toward the middle to shrink it, or tap S once with something selected to stay in scale mode until the next scale or Escape. S is scale whenever no line is being dragged.
asks before removing the selected parts, cells or line; a cell offers to take the parts inside it along.
undo and redo, up to sixty steps, before anything is saved.
saves everything you have changed; the drawing and its sibling .forge.json are both written, and nothing is saved until you press this or Save.

only while you are dragging a line: h drops a hook onto it, s a step, a an agent, d a store, u a screen, and the line carries on from the part you just dropped. The five letters are named on screen while the line is in your hand. At any other time they do nothing, which is why s on its own is scale. (There were six until 2026-09-10: **o** left the list when an output became a section of a cell's shell rather than a part you could drop on a line.)

opens the output shelf of whatever you have selected, a cell or its mouth: the loose fields the cell makes on the left, the packages already named on the right. A double-click on the mouth itself does the same.
picks a loose field for a package. Hold Alt and click as many as belong together, then name what they make and press Package; the boxes beside each field do the same thing for one at a time.
with a click adds to the selection; with a drag on empty canvas draws a selection box.
on a project in the list: keeps the one that is already open and opens this one beside it. A plain click opens one project at a time and closes the last, which is how both lists work now.

one step back at a time: cancels a line being drawn, then closes the output shelf, then the store's view, then the delete question, then leaves scale mode, then clears the selection. The shelf and the store's view each close three ways: this key, the close button on their head, or a press outside them.

masthead.what: The date, the slot you choose an instrument for (the day as a band, one project's track, or the week), the clock, the sessions running right now going round the sun, and the moon for the night agent.

mantra.what: One line a day under the date, picked from the date itself so it holds all day; hover it for another of today's.

next.what: One line: when the next call is, what it is and who is on it, with a press to join it and one into its call screen, or to write its prep when there is none.

chat.what: The conversation with the brain's agents, under Next: the last thing you asked and its answer, the box to send the next message with Enter, and a press for a new one.

command.what: One plain line to the main agent and nothing else: type it, press Enter, and the answer sits under it. The whole conversation is on the Chat page.

people.what: Everyone on your calendar between today and seven days out, with everyone the open items name, as bubbles or as a roll of names; a press opens their card.

horizon.what: Days left to each milestone this brain sets, as numerals or as a road.

opportunities.what: How many opportunities are in conversation and how many are live, with their kinds, opening the opportunities page.

moved.what: What changed in the brain, newest first, grouped by the hour, in the words of whoever changed it.

flow.what: The brain in the middle and everything it exchanges anything with around it, the apps, the calendar, GitHub and the rest, each line pulsing as the log is written.

system.what: A lamp for every part of the brain that runs on its own, with the last time each one ran under it.

in-progress.what: What is being made right now, one line for each piece of work, opening its thread.

work-threads.what: The pieces of work that run across the projects, each with how much waits on you, opening its thread.

deck.what: The questions waiting on you, one card at a time, the blocking ones first, answered right on the card. Off a new board: Today is where questions are answered.

decide.what: What is due today or already behind, each line a way into that item on Today, with the app's review queue at its foot. Off a new board.

dial.what: The sundial: the day drawn from sunrise to sunset with the sun where the hour is, today's calls on it, and the next call under it; it can show three days, the week or the month.

space.what: A gap on purpose, to give the instruments around it room.

tally.what: Three numbers: calls done of today's calls, your dated work done of what is on the clock, and questions answered of those waiting; as a sentence, bars or big figures.

status.what: How many parts of the brain write a status about themselves, and how old the oldest one is.

organize.what: The items sitting unsorted in a project's inbox, not yet put under a milestone.

stages.what: The build order: how far through the current milestone the work is, and what is next.

token-usage.what: The tokens each agent used, week by week over eight weeks, as stacked bars, so you can see whether something needs adjusting.

landed.what: The transcripts carrying today's date, and how many of them have been taken in.

threads.what: The standing call threads, the groups of people who meet on a cadence, with how much is open for each.

notepad.what: Your notes taken in this app, newest first, each opening in the Reader.

search.what: One box that finds a file in the brain by its name or by its words.

glossary.what: A door to the glossary: how many words it defines, one press to all of them.

running.what: The sessions with a turn in flight on this computer right now, and the helpers working under them.

live.what: One drawing from the Forge seen live: each part tied to what it stands for, lit by what moved in the last two weeks.

maps.what: The drawings of the brain, picked here, each opening in the Forge.

minimap.what: The brain drawn small as a constellation around the sun: projects on the inner ring, people and threads beyond, each as big as the work open on it and as bright as how lately it moved.

holons.what: How many parts the brain declares in its registry, and how many of their folders are really there.

mentee.what: How many stages the mentee programme has and how many pieces sit under them, opening the programme content page.
